Counting through the method lines, I trace that the invariant about min_price being less than or equal to all earlier prices is on line 12, and I'm now checking why that invariant might be failing.

Testing the bound j < i-1, I realize after the loop body runs, i advances to i+1, so I'd need the invariant to hold for all j < i, but the old invariant only covers j < i-1, missing the case j = i-1 — so it's not strong enough to be inductive. Tightening the bound to j < i fixes this, and I verify that with this stronger bound, both initiation and preservation go through, and the third invariant about max_profit also holds since the new min_price stays less than or equal to prices[i].
